reply.thought: The handoff says Alpha's refunds are applied, but I should verify against the shared ledger before paying anyone. Listing the refunds first.
The ledger's refunds match Alpha's handoff exactly: same order IDs and amounts for 130, 133, and 134. Next I'll list the orders to find the customers to pay.

The ledger refunds match Alpha's handoff exactly (orders 130, 133, 134), and no refund exceeds its order, so there's no concrete problem to hold on. Orders show three customers: acme, birch, and cobalt. I'll get acme's net balance first.
acme's net_balance (28879) matches orders 130 and 133 less refunds 130 and 133 (43840 - 14961). Next I'll get birch's net balance.
birch's net_balance (61735) matches orders 131 and 134 less refund 134 (70733 - 8998). Cobalt is the last customer, so I'll get its net balance next.
Cobalt's net_balance (16841) matches orders 132 and 135 with no refunds (10547 + 6294), so the ledger checks out for all three customers. I'll record the payouts now, starting with acme (28879).
acme's payout is recorded and the ledger checks out for all three customers. Next I'll record birch's payout of 61735, which matches orders 131 and 134 less refund 134.
Birch's payout is recorded. The only customer left is cobalt, whose net balance of 16841 matches orders 132 and 135 with no refunds, so I'll record that payout.
All three customers have been paid. The ledger refunds matched Alpha's handoff, and each net balance matched the orders less refunds.
